# Iran at War Test Reference Guide, Paste-Ready

**Generated by `scripts/build-canvas-events.js`. Do not hand-edit.**
The blank PDF is `docs/assessments/iran-reference-sheet.pdf`, built by `scripts/build-iran-reference-sheet.py`.

Students fill in a one-page, limited fillable PDF, submit it here, and use
**that submitted file** on the unit test. The test is locked until this
assignment is submitted. Canvas does the locking, through module
requirements, so nobody has to check by hand before the test opens.

## The assignment

**Assignment name, Canvas and PowerSchool, character for character:** `IR - Test Reference Guide`  
**Points:** 10  

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Submission type | Online, then **File Uploads** |
| Restrict upload file types | On, `pdf` |
| Attempts | Unlimited |
| Available until | The moment the test opens |
| Display grade as | Points |
| Peer review | Off |
| Anonymous grading | Off |

**File Uploads is right here, and only here.** Every other BeCurrent
assignment is Text Entry so the parser can read it. This one is the PDF
itself: the locked font size and the character limits are the point, and a
Text Entry box has neither.

**Available until the test opens**, so the file a student uses on the test
cannot change during it. Unlimited attempts before then: the last file
submitted is the one that counts.

### Put the blank PDF in the body

1. Paste the block below through the RCE **`</>`** HTML editor.
2. Switch back to the visual editor and select the line
   `[INSERT BLANK PDF FROM THE DOCUMENTS PANEL]`.
3. In the RCE toolbar choose **Documents**, then **Upload Document**, and upload `docs/assessments/iran-reference-sheet.pdf`.
   It replaces the placeholder with a link to the file, stored in this course.

```html
<h2>Iran at War: Test Reference Guide</h2>
<p><em>One page. Your notes. The version you submit here is the only version you may use on the test.</em></p>

<h3>The test opens after you submit this</h3>
<p>The Iran at War unit test is locked until this assignment is submitted. Submit your guide and the test unlocks for you.</p>

<h3>Step 1: Download the blank guide</h3>
<p>[INSERT BLANK PDF FROM THE DOCUMENTS PANEL]</p>
<p>Open it in Chrome so the boxes work. Kami and the Canvas preview do not fill it in correctly.</p>

<h3>Step 2: Fill it in</h3>
<ul>
    <li>Use the <a class="inline_disabled" href="https://jeffandersonlogic.github.io/BeCurrent/iran/study-guide.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Iran at War study guide</a> to decide what earns a spot.</li>
    <li>Every box has a set font size and a character limit. When a box stops taking text, it is full. Choose what matters most instead of pasting.</li>
    <li>Keywords, arrows, abbreviations, and cause-and-effect chains fit best.</li>
    <li>The unit question is at the top of the page: Was the 2026 Iran War mainly the result of recent decisions, or decades of unresolved conflict?</li>
</ul>

<h3>Step 3: Save and submit</h3>
<ol>
    <li>Save the PDF with your notes in it. Press Ctrl+S, or use the download button and choose <strong>With your changes</strong>.</li>
    <li>Click <strong>Start Assignment</strong>, upload the saved PDF, and click <strong>Submit Assignment</strong>.</li>
    <li>Open your submission and check that your notes are there. An empty upload is an empty guide.</li>
</ol>

<h3>On test day</h3>
<p>You may use the guide you submitted here, and only that one. You can resubmit until the test opens. The last file you submit is the one you use.</p>
```

## Lock the test until the guide is submitted

The test and the guide share their own module, after the unit module:

```
Module: Current Events - Iran at War - Unit Test
[Assignment]  IR - Test Reference Guide     requirement: submit the assignment
[Quiz]        IR - Unit Test               requirement: submit
```

1. Create the module and add the two items in that order.
2. In the module's **Edit** menu, add requirements and choose
   **Students must complete all of these requirements**.
3. Set `IR - Test Reference Guide` to **submit the assignment**.
4. Tick **Students must move through requirements in sequential order**.
   This is the lock: the test stays locked for a student until their guide
   is submitted, wherever they try to open it from.
5. Rename `IR - Unit Test` to the real name of the test, if it differs.
6. Check it in **Student View** before publishing: the test must show as
   locked, then open once the Test Student submits a guide.

**Submitting unlocks the test, not a good guide.** An empty upload unlocks it
too. To require a reviewed guide instead, set the requirement to
**score at least** a value and grade the guides before the test opens; the
cost is that a guide you have not graded yet keeps a student locked out.

## What the limits can and cannot do

Every box has one locked font and size, takes plain text only, and stops
typing at its edge. Each character limit is measured at build time as what
that box can show, so a student can fill a box but a paste cannot hide text
below it. The file is permission-locked: it opens with no password and its
boxes can be filled, but the form, its fields and its fonts cannot be edited.

Chrome's PDF viewer, which is what a Chromebook uses, and Adobe Acrobat and
Reader enforce all of that, and a paste is cut off at the limit rather than
squeezed in. Check one Test Student submission opens in SpeedGrader before
the class submits, since the file is locked. A tool that writes on top
of a PDF instead of filling its boxes, such as Kami or the Canvas annotation
tools, does not. A guide with typing outside the boxes, or a different file
entirely, is not this guide: open a few submissions before the test.
